newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Digitel eyes public mobile phone system.
newsitem.headline: Digitel eyes public mobile phone system.

text.p: Digital Telecommunications Phils. Inc, the telecommunications arm of JG Summit Holdings Inc, said on Monday it will join the government's bidding next year to operate a personal communications network (PCN) nationwide.

"We will participate in the bidding for nationwide PCN," William Pamintuan, Digitel senior vice-president told Reuters. A PCN is a cheaper form of mobile telephone which is yet to be introduced in the Philippines.
The National Telecommunications Communications (NTC) is planning to hold a bidding by the first quarter of 1997 for the frequency bands for the public mobile telephone service which includes PCN.
The NTC has divided the Philippines into four service zones where a maximum of two carriers shall be authorised to operate a public mobile telephone service in each zone.

These zones are the entire northern island of Luzon excluding the National Capital Region, the National Capital Region itself, central Visayas island and the entire Mindanao area in southern Philippines.

The NTC is presently conducting public hearings on the guidelines on how to allocate the frequency bands. The regulatory body was planning to require winning bidders per zone to put up 150,000 lines in exchange for their permit to operate a public mobile phone system.
